items.sentence: Today’s episode is a deepdive into the day-to-day tools of devs at Uber, our tour guide being on of Uber’s longest-tenured engineers: Uday Kiran Medisetty.
Uber’s service count changed erratically: in 2015, when Uday joined, there were two services in total.
M3DB: Uber was emitting about 500 million metrics per second, with no vendor being able to handle this load, so they built it themselves.
Morpheus: a system combining feature flags and experimentation, including switchback tests, with support for two- and three-sided marketplaces that Uber operates.
AIFX allows engineers to switch harnesses without losing settings.
Before, it would take so much time to create a PR, so you would be laser-focused on it.
But now you’re constantly switching between so many things.
You need to be able to verify your work and pick any code smells from the agent [to avoid] shipping regressions into production.

Uber’s AI tooling was seemingly built in a year: in reality, it was built on top of a decade worth of dev tooling investment.
Minion – built in 2025 – is powered by DevPods, which Uber created in 2017.
